origin.description: Replace matches in mode first, all, or last by calling the matching replacer.
origin.usage: stri_replace(str, replacement, ..., regex, fixed, coll, charclass, mode = c("first", "all", "last"))

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Character vector of replacements for the matched patterns.

arguments.name: regex, fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: One of regex, fixed, coll, or charclass. Exactly one must be supplied. NULL is a supplied empty pattern. A missing argument is not supplied.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.text: One of "first" (the default), "all", or "last". A unique prefix is accepted. NULL selects first.
Further arguments forwarded to the chosen mode function, including settings merged into opts_regex, opts_fixed, or opts_collator.

origin.details: Exactly one of regex, fixed, coll, and charclass must be supplied. An explicit NULL is supplied and searches with an empty pattern. Omitting every pattern argument is an error, and so is supplying two. Arguments in ... are passed to the chosen function. A name that follows ... is not partially matched, so reg does not select regex. mode is first, all, or last. The default is first. match.arg accepts a unique prefix. NULL and a missing mode are first. The three documented choices together also select first. mode is resolved before the pattern arguments are checked. A missing replacement is an error only after one pattern argument has been accepted.
origin.example:
result <- stri_replace("Lorem ipsum dolor", "#", fixed = "or")
cat(paste0('stri_replace("Lorem ipsum dolor", "#", fixed = "or") returns ', result, '.\n'))

translation.description: Replace matches in mode first, all, or last by calling the matching replacer.
translation.usage: stri_replace(str, replacement=..., *args, regex=..., fixed=..., coll=..., charclass=..., mode=..., **kwargs)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty replacement and returns an empty list.

arguments.name: regex, fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: One of regex, fixed, coll, or charclass. Exactly one must be supplied. None is a supplied empty pattern. Omitting the argument is a different state.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.text: One of "first" (the default), "all", or "last". A unique prefix is accepted. None selects first.
Further keywords forwarded to the chosen mode function. The mode functions already accept those opts_* settings.

translation.details: An omitted pattern argument is a private sentinel, and None is an explicit NULL passed on as an empty list. Extra keywords, including case_insensitive, strength, negate, n, and the opts_* lists, are forwarded to the mode function. A short name such as reg is not treated as regex. mode is first, all, or last. A missing mode and None are first. A unique prefix such as a or las is accepted. The list first, all, last selects first. A bad mode is an error before the pattern arguments are checked. A missing replacement is an error only after one pattern argument has been accepted.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing string stays NA. An empty pattern or replacement returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.dispatch import stri_replace
result = stri_replace("Lorem ipsum dolor", "#", fixed="or")
print(f'stri_replace("Lorem ipsum dolor", "#", fixed="or") returns {result[0]}.')
